lead.headline: CYCLONE ARNAB MAKES LANDFALL; FLOODING REPORTED IN ANDHRA
lead.deck: The storm crossed the coast near Yanam with destructive winds as heavy rain hit coastal districts

image.alt: Cyclone Arnab bringing heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh
image.caption: The landfall process began overnight between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. (ANI / Moneycontrol)

paragraphs: Five people, including four members of the same family, were killed in a shooting at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati. A sixth person was injured and taken for treatment.
Guwahati Police said the suspect was arrested within an hour and the firearm was seized. Investigators said preliminary findings point to a dispute linked to the hotel lease.
Police said the inquiry is at an early stage, with forensic teams examining the scene and further details pending. The suspect had leased the property, according to investigators.
Police said the firing began at about 9 pm during a meeting linked to the hotel. Six people were shot; five later died, while the survivor was taken for treatment.
A six-member Special Investigation Team was formed the following day to examine the shooting and the dispute over the hotel’s lease and management.

sidebarStory.headline: LEOPARD CUB RESCUED NEAR BENGALURU AS SIGHTINGS RISE
sidebarStory.subhead: A month-old cub was found in a Nelamangala farm; villagers report leopard activity near homes
paragraphs: Forest officials rescued a month-old male leopard cub from farmland in Mallarabanavadi, Nelamangala taluk, after it was found separated from its mother. Villagers have also reported adult leopard sightings near homes and attacks on domestic animals.

stories.headline: CYCLONE CANCELLATIONS HIT BENGALURU-LINKED FLIGHTS
stories.subhead: Air India Express scrubbed services linking Visakhapatnam with Bengaluru and other cities
paragraphs: Flight operations were suspended at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry airports as Cyclone Arnab approached. Air India Express cancelled 13 flights, including services connecting Visakhapatnam with Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Vijayawada. Passengers were advised to check directly with their airline.

stories.headline: CM SAYS KPSC WILL BE GIVEN A NEW FORM
stories.subhead: Forest team moved the month-old animal to Bannerghatta rehabilitation centre
paragraphs: A month-old male leopard cub found alone in farmland at Mallarabanavadi was rescued and taken to the Bannerghatta Rehabilitation Centre. Forest officials had not confirmed whether the cub’s mother was located.

stories.headline: THREE ANDHRA AIRPORTS SUSPEND FLIGHTS AS STORM ARRIVES
paragraphs: Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry airports suspended operations during Cyclone Arnab, with airlines cancelling services as a safety measure.

stories.headline: HENNUR-BAGALUR ROAD WORK GETS TWO-MONTH DEADLINE
stories.subhead: A second contractor will be brought in to accelerate the delayed concretising project
paragraphs: Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda set a two-month deadline for the Hennur-Bagalur Road works and directed officials to add another contractor. The project will also extend from 4.6km to 5km.

stories.headline: SARJAPUR COMMUTERS BACK PREMIUM BMTC BUSES
stories.subhead: Survey respondents asked for reliable frequency, air-conditioning and live bus tracking
paragraphs: A BMTC and Save Our Sarjapur survey found 73.1% of respondents would pay a premium for buses with air-conditioning, comfortable seats, Wi-Fi and fixed schedules. The report also highlighted gaps in bus tracking and transfers.

stories.headline: CITY SCREENING FINDS HEALTH RISKS AMONG FRONTLINE WORKERS
stories.subhead: A three-year programme covered more than 10,000 workers exposed to traffic and construction pollution
paragraphs: A Bengaluru occupational-health screening found respiratory and cardiometabolic risks among BMTC staff, traffic police, construction workers and pourakarmikas. Experts called for stronger workplace healthcare and follow-through on the findings.

stories.headline: ARNAB’S LANDFALL BRINGS FLOODING AND 135-KMPH WINDS
stories.deck: Authorities report heavy rain and rescues as the storm crosses the coast near Yanam

image.alt: Cyclone Arnab brings rain to Andhra Pradesh
image.caption: The storm’s landfall process began overnight on the Andhra coast. (ANI / Moneycontrol)

paragraphs: Cyclone Arnab began making landfall around 1:20 am between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near south Yanam. The process was expected to continue for several hours.
Winds were reported at 125–135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph. Heavy rain and flooding affected coastal districts including Kakinada, while police rescued four people stranded in floodwater.

stories.headline: GOVT PROMISES SUPPORT AFTER LUCKNOW TRIPLE MURDER
paragraphs: Uttar Pradesh’s government promised a job for the widow and free education for the couple’s daughter after three men were shot dead in Lucknow following a parking dispute. Officials also announced security support and said NSA action would be pursued against the accused.

stories.headline: NDA WINS ALL FOUR KARNATAKA MLC SEATS
paragraphs: The BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats for teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies, including the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat. The results were reported on October 28.

stories.headline: FINAL KARNATAKA ROLL SHOWS 99.76 LAKH FEWER ELECTORS
paragraphs: The final electoral roll lists 4.55 crore electors, down 99.76 lakh from the pre-revision count. Officials said the revision also added a net 8.19 lakh electors during claims and objections.

stories.headline: LEOPARD SIGHTINGS RISE NEAR BENGALURU; CUB RESCUED
stories.deck: Forest officials found a month-old cub in a Nelamangala farm as villages report leopard activity
paragraphs: A month-old male leopard cub was rescued from agricultural land in Mallarabanavadi village, Nelamangala taluk, after it was found separated from its mother. It was taken to the Bannerghatta Rehabilitation Centre.
Residents have reported adult leopard sightings near homes and attacks on domestic animals. Villagers have sought capture measures; officials had not said whether the cub’s mother was found.

stories.headline: ARNAB DISRUPTS FLIGHTS LINKING BENGALURU AND VIZAG
paragraphs: Air India Express cancelled 13 flights as three Andhra airports suspended operations during the cyclone. The cancellations included services connecting Visakhapatnam with Bengaluru.

stories.headline: LUCKNOW TRIPLE MURDER: GOVT ANNOUNCES FAMILY SUPPORT
paragraphs: The state promised a government job for the widow and free education for her daughter after three men were killed in a shooting linked to a parking dispute.

stories.headline: KIA TESTS DIGI YATRA FOR INTERNATIONAL DEPARTURES
paragraphs: Kempegowda International Airport has begun trials of face-enabled Digi Yatra processing for select international departures on IndiGo and Air India. Passengers must still carry travel documents and complete immigration checks.

stories.headline: BJP RETAINS THREE UP COUNCIL SEATS; SP WINS VARANASI
stories.deck: Counting continues in the state Legislative Council polls

image.caption: Results emerged from the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections. (Representative image)

paragraphs: The BJP retained three seats in Uttar Pradesh’s Legislative Council elections, while the Samajwadi Party retained the Varanasi teachers’ constituency. Counting remained underway in other contests.

listing: BJP retains in UP council polls

stories.headline: UP GOVT OFFERS WIDOW JOB AFTER TRIPLE MURDER
paragraphs: The government announced employment, education and security support for the family of three men killed in a Lucknow shooting after a parking dispute.

stories.headline: ABHISHEK SHARMA BLASTS 113 FROM 38 BALLS
paragraphs: Abhishek Sharma hit a 38-ball century as India overwhelmed New Zealand in the second T20I, according to the match report.

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT CLEARS WAY FOR BLUE LINE WORK AT HEBBAL
stories.deck: The ruling removes a legal hurdle for construction near the airport corridor
paragraphs: The Supreme Court has cleared the way for work on Bengaluru Metro’s Blue Line project near Hebbal, according to a report published on October 27. The corridor is planned to connect central Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport.
The decision addresses a dispute that had held up work in the area. Project timelines and the pace of construction will depend on the next steps by the metro authority and contractors.

stories.headline: CONSTRUCTION COSTS RISE 33% AS SALES SLOW
paragraphs: Builders in Bengaluru are facing tighter margins as construction costs rise and home sales slow, a Times of India report said. Developers described pressure from higher input costs alongside a softer market.

stories.headline: 500 KM OF NEW ROADS PLANNED FOR BENGALURU
paragraphs: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the state plans 500 kilometres of new roads in Bengaluru, according to a report published on October 27.

stories.headline: MATERIAL SHORTAGE ADDS PRESSURE TO BLUE LINE WORK
paragraphs: Contractors on the 58-kilometre Blue Line have reported shortages of quarry dust, crushed stone and aggregates after a Tamil Nadu transport ban disrupted supplies. The shortage has affected construction and depot work.

stories.headline: ‘GONDHAL’ TRAILER DEBUTS AHEAD OF SEVEN-LANGUAGE RELEASE
stories.deck: India’s Oscar entry is set for a worldwide theatrical release on November 13
paragraphs: The psychological thriller Gondhal has unveiled its global trailer ahead of a November 13 theatrical release. The film, India’s official submission for the 99th Academy Awards’ Best International Feature Film category, is planned in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada and English.
Directed by Santosh Davakhar, the story follows newlyweds whose lives take a disturbing turn as family pressures and devotion collide. The film draws on Maharashtra’s cultural traditions.

stories.headline: SHIVARAJKUMAR JOINS NIRUP BHANDARI’S ‘SATHYA’
paragraphs: Shivarajkumar has joined the cast of the comedy-drama Sathya: Son of Harishchandra, starring Nirup Bhandari. The film’s lead character is written as an ardent fan of Shivanna, making the veteran actor’s part central to the story.

stories.headline: ‘HUBBALLI HUNTERS’ SETS DECEMBER 11 RELEASE
paragraphs: The Kannada film Hubballi Hunters is scheduled to open across Karnataka on December 11. Rishab Shetty Music has acquired the audio rights; the film’s score is composed by Prasanna Keshava.

stories.headline: LAYA KOKILA’S ‘THAYTHA’ OPENS OCTOBER 30
paragraphs: Laya Kokila’s directorial debut Thaytha is set to release in Karnataka on October 30. The filmmaker describes it as a love story with comedy and thriller elements.
